objective: Recover only D0-D32 assets that strengthen the single-controller FME mainline without restoring failed branch representations, one-off experiment runners, API artifacts or raw responses.
selection_criteria: The asset strengthens the unique FMEResearchLoop, a real multi-problem adapter seam, falsifiable memory, evidence identity or replayability.
The asset remains useful after the scientific branch that produced it is falsified.
The asset is problem-neutral or explicitly isolated behind an adapter.
The asset does not activate a historical cohort or expose heldout evidence.
The asset can be statically inspected without restoring API reports, raw responses or large experiment logs.

retained_code.reason: Pure deterministic one-action research loop with frozen contract, budget reservation, injected action adapters and hash-bound decisions.
Three concrete BP, TSP and CVRP adapters make the challenge-validity seam real and keep problem fields out of the controller interface.
Counterevidence produces immutable claim transitions and a controller-readable development-only summary.
Action and outcome receipts preserve one selected action, one terminal outcome and actor identity without storing prompts, code or responses.
Restores ORF-001 through ORF-005 identity binding, complete-summary validation, cache attribution, failure hashing and exact-tie admission corrections.
Converts invalid order-regime evidence contracts into an explicit projection failure instead of accepting partial evidence.
Adds an explicit depth-first profile that lets accepted counterevidence outrank historical reliability and transfer controls without adding a new scientific action.
Makes problem identity explicit and exposes action/outcome receipt recording through the existing recorder seam.

retained_findings: D0: evidence identity, initial-population projection and verifier binding are mainline integrity requirements; historical static acceptance is not treated as a current test pass.

D1: the historical CVRP runtime demonstrated an action-receipt to accepted-counterexample to existing-claim transition to repair-action chain under heldout isolation; current restored code has not replayed that result.

D2: masking counterexample and weakened-claim evidence changed repair/m1 to invent/e1, but all six candidates remained in one intrinsic behavior cell, so action-path change is not algorithm-quality evidence.
D3-D7: robust archive geometry was supported, but parent exposure, generation regularization and useful novelty were not; behavior_cover must remain excluded and inactive.
D8-D32: positive single-decision CVRP interventions did not compose into endpoint-valid global or stateless sparse policies; local witness compatibility is not a sufficient policy representation.
explicitly_excluded: all D0-D32 manifests and API reports
the rejected coarse behavior_cell archive-key modification
D21-D25 repair-and-invent, portfolio cooldown and robust-selection activation
raw prompts, raw responses, credentials, caches and experiment logs
current_limits: No historical verifier, replay, import, test suite, build, candidate evaluation, API call or LLM call was executed during recovery.
Historical D1 and D2 results remain evidence about the archived implementation and are not reclassified as validation of the current worktree.
The restored pure modules are available for targeted integration but do not authorize a new cohort.
No algorithm-quality, heldout-generalization or cross-problem-superiority claim is accepted.
next_gate: Perform static diff and contract inspection, then wait for explicit approval before any targeted compile, replay or test execution.
